Hi Tessa,

We're finalizing FY28 capital plans and are evaluating prepay options for inference spend. Subject: RE: Budgetary ask: FY28 prepay + multi-year ramp

Tessa / Ben — draft numbers below (budgetary, not final legal):

Scenario A — 12-month prepay
- Annual commitment: $480,000
- Effective unit discount: 7%
- Invoice split options: 100% upfront (standard) or 50% upfront + 50% 6 months in
- Unused committed token credit: available as rolling credit for 12 months (no cash refund)

Scenario B — 3-year commit (preferred economics)
- Year 1 commit: $420,000 (baseline capacity)
- Year 2 commit: $525,000 (ramp to higher throughput)
- Year 3 commit: $630,000 (full scale)
- Multi-year discounted rate: 14% blended across term vs list
- Ramp profile we recommend modeling: 45% / 80% / 100% of final throughput (conservative front-load) — but pricing above assumes the stepped commit schedule shown.
- Invoicing cadence: 30% upfront (year 1), then quarterly billing on recognized usage vs committed baseline. We can flip to upfront of 50% if finance needs larger upfront.

Notes: We can include a Monte Carlo-style credit rebalancing clause in the contract to allow modest overage smoothing. Also include a one-time onboarding credit of $12,000 applied as a token credit at contract signature if they commit to 3 years.

I'll assemble a pro forma PDF and an XLS with line-item invoice splits and sample cashflow timings. ETA: EOD Thu Nov 26.

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance — Redwood Dedicated

Hi Olivia — quick note from the delivery side. If Horizon wants to start Q1 with Clinical NLP + Summarization, we should lock baseline capacity by Dec 31 to ensure GPU pool availability and to honor the quoted rates. For the 3-year model:

- If you want the staged ramp you described (40/30/30 across years), it’s fine — we'll reserve additional burst capacity, but pricing above was modeled for the 45/80/100 ramp; smaller initial ramp reduces early-year costs but increases later-year unit rate marginally.

I'll coordinate capacity reservation once we have a signed PO and initial invoice timing. Let me know if you need a short note explaining how reserved capacity vs burst works for procurement.
